reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is physically sound in principle (increased contact area reduces thermal boundary resistance), but it overlooks that at 600–1500°C, surface diffusion and creep will rapidly degrade nanoscale trenches, and the proposed (CrFeTiTa)70W30 alloy may form brittle intermetallics, compromising structural integrity.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is detailed and includes a clear falsification criterion (2× reduction in thermal boundary resistance and no mechanical degradation), but the nanosecond-transient thermoreflectance measurement on a bonded, multi-layer stack under simulated reactor conditions is extremely challenging and may not isolate the interface resistance cleanly.
reasons.usefulness: The idea of surface patterning to enhance heat transfer is a creative, non-obvious intervention for this application, and even if the specific implementation is flawed, it could stimulate useful research on interface engineering for plasma-facing components.
